data.standardized_narrative: The report does not quantify a gross prior-year reserve movement. Gross claims outstanding increased from 139.4 (at 31 Dec 2021) to 225.9 (at 31 Dec 2022) (both in report currency), reflecting an overall increase in gross reserves largely driven by recent natural catastrophe activity and geopolitical impacts. The syndicate did not provide a separate gross prioryear development figure; therefore prior-year development is not separately quantified in the accounts. Primary drivers called out were climate-related natural catastrophe events (Hurricanes Ida and Ian, Storms Uri and Elliot, flooding, Volker hail) and the war in Ukraine.
raw_causal_phrases: the 2021 underwriting year has been impacted by a number of climate related natural catastrophes such as Hurricanes Ida and Ian, Storms Uri and Elliot, various flooding catastrophes and the Volker hail event.
The war in Ukraine has also impacted the 2022 underwriting year.

Despite this challenging claims environment the syndicate is expected to produce a positive return on capacity for 2021 underwriting year - indicating that such events are within the syndicate's expected range.

data.data_quality_notes: No explicit gross prior-year movement (movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding) is disclosed in the provided notes or narrative. The technical provisions note provides opening and closing gross claims outstanding and the total gross movement during the year, but that 'movement in the provision' includes current year claims movements and cannot be used as a prior-year development figure per the extraction rules. A gross prior-year movement figure was not found; prior-year development is therefore reported as null. All monetary figures are in the report's native currency (USD).
